title: Badshahi Mosque
credits: Photos: Saqib Rubab, Jamshaid Mughal, Hassaan Malik / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: In the heart of old Lahore stands one of the great monuments of the Mughal Empire.
This is the Badshahi Mosque, the royal mosque.
It was commissioned by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.
Work was completed in sixteen seventy-three, more than three hundred and fifty years ago.
Its walls are built of red sandstone, carved and inlaid with white marble.
Above them rise three great white marble domes.
Tall minarets stand at each corner, watching over the city.
For centuries, it stood among the largest mosques in the world.
Its vast courtyard was built to hold tens of thousands of worshippers at once.
It faces the Lahore Fort, across the gardens of the Hazuri Bagh.
And beside its steps lies the tomb of Allama Iqbal, Pakistan's national poet.
Today, it remains one of the proudest landmarks of Lahore, and of Pakistan.
